# Navigation and docs.json

`docs.json` should reproduce the source site's structure and chrome, nothing more. Look up the current schema at https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/settings.md before writing it.

## Build navigation from the source's nav data

Most platforms publish their sidebar as data (a sidebar file, `SUMMARY.md`, a nav key in the config, a JSON payload). Use it instead of inferring structure from folders. The source guide names it (`mint migrate --from <name>`); for anything else, use the rendered sidebar of each section.

Walk that tree and emit Mintlify's shape, keeping group order, labels and nesting depth verbatim. Leaf URLs become repo-relative paths without `.mdx`. Generate `docs.json` with a script past about 50 pages.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/navigation.md

Only when the source has no nav data and no readable sidebar, fall back to the directory tree: one group per directory, the directory's index or overview page first, titles from the source.

Fetch sidebars as raw HTML (`curl`) and parse the list structure. Text-only page summaries flatten nested groups and lose the hierarchy.

## Structure rules

- **Nesting.** A sidebar entry with children is a nested group: `{ "group": "Parent", "pages": ["parent/index", "parent/child"] }`. The parent page goes first and gets `sidebarTitle: "Overview"` only if the source labels it that way; otherwise keep its source label. Never flatten children into siblings.
- **Per-tab sidebars.** Each top-level section with its own sidebar becomes a tab (or product) with its own `groups`, mirroring that section's sidebar. Pages not in a section's source sidebar do not go in that tab. Never dump leftovers into a catch-all "Reference" or "Misc" group.
- **Surfaces.** Use root `groups`, `tabs`, `products` and `versions` the way the source presents its sections. From source code, use exactly what the code declares.
- **No invented icons.** Add `icon` to tabs, groups or pages only where the source shows an icon.
- **External links in the top row** stay in the same surface as the rest of the row: `{ "tab": "Status", "href": "https://..." }`.
- **Orphans.** Every converted page appears in navigation exactly once. If the source had pages reachable only by link, ask the user where they belong or put them in `"hidden": true` groups, and report it.
- **Versions and languages** map to `navigation.versions` / `navigation.languages` only if the user chose to migrate them.
- **Untranslated locale pages.** If the source served default-language content at `/<locale>/page` for pages with no translation, do not create duplicate pages: redirect each such URL to the default-language page and report the list.

Hidden pages: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/hidden-pages.md

## Reconstructed navigation

Only when scraping, where no code declares the navigation (`mint migrate --topic discovery`, Get the source):

- Put each section's landing or overview page first in its group.
- Keep the site root `index` out of sidebar groups unless the source shows a Home row.
- Flatten a single-page group whose label duplicates the page's title.
- Put icons on top-level sections only.
- Set `expanded: false` only on nested groups, and only when the source's sections were collapsible.
- Do not add tabs or switchers just to fill the header.

With source code, never apply these where they would change what the code declares. If the declared navigation looks broken, report it instead of restructuring.

## Chrome

Default is remove. Add each element only after confirming it on the source:

- `name`, `logo` (light and dark), `favicon`, `colors.primary`: from the source site. Download the files.
- `navbar.links`: only the right-hand utility links the source shows.
- `navbar.primary`: only if the source has a CTA button.
- `navigation.global.anchors`: only if the source has a persistent anchor list at the top of the sidebar.
- `footer.socials` and `footer.links`: only what the source footer shows.
- `seo.metatags`: mirror the source's meta tags where Mintlify supports them.

`mint init` and templates add starter defaults (example anchors, social links, CTA buttons, placeholder colors). Remove every default the source does not have. Each chrome item lives in exactly one surface; nothing appears in both `navigation.tabs` and `navbar.links`.

Analytics, search, feedback widgets, custom scripts and custom CSS do not migrate automatically. List them in the report with what Mintlify offers instead.

Mintlify loads every `.css` and `.js` file in the content directory on every page; scripts run everywhere except the editor's live preview. Selectors and scripts written for the old theme's DOM match nothing: port only real brand rules. Delete MathJax, KaTeX and Mermaid loaders; Mintlify renders math and Mermaid natively.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/settings-structure.md, https://www.mintlify.com/docs/customize/custom-scripts.md

## Redirects

Every source URL must keep working. Write redirects to `redirects.json` at the project root and reference it from `docs.json` with `"redirects": { "$ref": "./redirects.json" }`. If `docs.json` already has inline `redirects`, move them into the file. For each page whose path changes, add an entry:

```json
[{ "source": "/old/path", "destination": "/new/path" }]
```

Include old trailing-slash forms if the source served them, removed sections the user wants to point somewhere, and per-entry changelog URLs. Do not redirect a path to itself, and do not chain redirects. A redirect source can be `/`.

- **Wildcards.** Nothing matches a suffix and there is no regex.
- **`.html` URLs.** When the old site served `/a/b.html`, add one exact redirect per page from `/a/b.html` to `/a/b`, generated from the old build output or sitemap. Skip index URLs that still resolve.
- **Base path.** If every old URL sat under a prefix (`baseUrl`, `basePath`, `base`, `routeBasePath`) that the Mintlify site drops, add one `/<prefix>/:slug*` → `/:slug*` redirect.
- **Existing redirect config.** Port the source's own redirects: static pairs and trailing `:name*` patterns carry over; temporary redirects get `"permanent": false`. A single-segment `:name` (no `*`) is matched literally, so expand it, and entries using regex, query or header conditions, into exact paths, or report them.
- **Hash and query URLs.** Fragments and query strings never reach the server, so no redirect can match them. Pin heading ids instead (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Heading IDs) and report the rest.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/create/redirects.md, https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/settings.md

## Check the file

After every structural edit run `mint validate`. Then compare navigation against disk, on any route: every `.mdx` is listed exactly once, with no missing pages, dangling paths or duplicates. Collect page strings recursively from `tabs`, `products`, `versions`, `groups` and `pages`; never count `group` or `tab` labels as page paths.
